extracted.intended_audience: general readers, journalists, and researchers interested in the Costa Concordia disaster and maritime safety
extracted.subtask_description: A detailed encyclopedic article documenting the Costa Concordia shipwreck, its salvage, legal proceedings, industry and regulatory responses, and safety-related requirements invoked or changed by the incident.

rubrics_metrics.name: IMO muster and survival-craft timing requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Passenger ships are subject to International Maritime Organization requirements to perform 'musters of the passengers (...) within 24 hours after their embarkation' and to be able to launch 'survival craft' sufficient for 'the total number of persons aboard ... within a period of 30 minutes from the time the abandon-ship signal is given'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are international regulatory minima referenced to assess compliance in evacuations and lifesaving preparedness; failure to meet these timings is a regulatory safety failure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lifeboat capacity and hard-lifeboat proportion
rubrics_metrics.description: Passenger ships must be equipped with lifeboats for 125% of the ship's passenger and crew maximum capacity, among which at least 37.5% of that capacity on each side of the ship (75% of total) must consist of hard lifeboats as opposed to inflatable ones.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Capacity and type proportions are prescriptive design/fit-out standards used to judge whether a vessel met lifesaving equipment requirements at the time of an incident.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lifeboat launching system performance (list and pitch limits)
rubrics_metrics.description: Launching systems must enable the lowering of the lifeboats under 20° of list and 10° of pitch.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This specifies operational limits for safe lifeboat deployment; incidents where list/pitch exceed these angles may prevent successful launching and indicate either equipment or procedural failings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Crew Basic Safety Training and evacuation drill frequency (internal policy)
rubrics_metrics.description: According to Costa Cruises, its internal regulations require all crew members to complete Basic Safety Training, and to perform a ship evacuation drill every two weeks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frequency of drills and baseline training are internal company standards cited to evaluate preparedness and whether internal policies were followed prior to the accident.

rubrics_metrics.name: Routine lifeboat launch testing
rubrics_metrics.description: Every week, all the lifeboats on one side of the ship are launched for a test.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Routine practical tests are an operational maintenance/verification practice to ensure lifeboats and launch systems function; failure to conduct such tests could be cited as contributory to evacuation problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ship design survivability standard (compartment flooding)
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the regulations in force in 2006 when Costa Concordia was delivered, the ship had to be designed to survive the flooding of two adjacent compartments caused by an 11-metre (36 ft) breach.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a construction/design regulatory criterion used to assess whether the vessel's watertight subdivision and damage stability met statutory requirements and whether the actual damage exceeded design assumptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Muster drill timing and pre-departure muster requirement (industry policy change)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Cruise Lines International Association (CLIA), the European Cruise Council (ECC) and the Passenger Shipping Association adopted a new policy requiring all embarking passengers to participate in muster drills before departure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Post-incident industry policy change used as a benchmark for updated passenger safety practice; contrasts with prior practice allowing musters within 24 hours of embarkation.

rubrics_metrics.name: New muster policy content (12 specific emergency instructions)
rubrics_metrics.description: The new muster policy consists of 12 specific emergency instructions, which include providing information on when and how to don a life jacket, where to muster and what to expect if there is an evacuation of the ship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies minimum informational content of passenger safety briefings; used to evaluate adequacy of passenger instruction and preparedness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bridge-route and bridge-access procedural requirements (CLIA/ECC policies)
rubrics_metrics.description: On 24 April, the CLIA and the ECC introduced new policies: bridge officers must agree on the route before departing; ships must carry more lifejackets; and access to the bridge must be limited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedural controls to reduce navigational errors and unauthorized bridge presence; these are governance/operational criteria for safe navigation and command integrity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compensation package for uninjured passengers (Costa offer)
rubrics_metrics.description: Costa posted a compensation package offering €11,000 per person to compensate for all damages (including loss of baggage and property, psychological distress, loss of enjoyment of the cruise) and reimbursement for a range of other costs and losses, including value of the cruise, air and bus travel costs included in the cruise package, travel expenses to return home, medical expenses arising from the event, and expenses incurred on board during the cruise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This corporate compensation policy and its scope/timeliness (offer effective until 31 March 2012) are standards for assessing corporate liability mitigation and passenger remediation; families of dead/missing were to be offered separate proposals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Crew compensation and post-incident wage/reimbursement terms
rubrics_metrics.description: The trade union representing the crew negotiated compensation packages: crew members were paid wages for a minimum of two months or, if longer, their full contract term; they also received reimbursement for expenses and up to £2,250 for lost personal property.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employment/compensation terms used to evaluate company response to crew welfare and contractual obligations after an incident.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emergency disembarkation statutory/operational compensation threshold
rubrics_metrics.description: After certain emergency disembarkations and other events, the cruise ship operator is required to compensate passengers €10,000 each.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulatory or industry-stated compensation thresholds that can be invoked following emergency disembarkation; used as a benchmark for passenger redress.

rubrics_metrics.name: Salvage-site remediation project scope and budget
rubrics_metrics.description: Costa Crociere put Micoperi in charge of the salvage site remediation (phase WP9). Initially, $85 million was assigned to the project, to start end of 2014 and take about 15 months; main activities included ocean floor cleaning, anchor block removal, grout bag removal, and platform removal. The project continued into May 2018 with regular publication of activity details.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets expectations for remediation work scope, schedule, budgeting, and public reporting practices used to evaluate adequacy of environmental/salvage remediation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recorded-evidence / voyage-data-recorder (VDR) recovery and analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the ship's voyage data recorders (VDRs), which was designed to float, was recovered; others were located later or were hard to reach. Data storage devices and hard disks (including camera footage from the control board) were recovered and expected to reveal movements of the ship's captain and officers. Specialists were ordered to review VDR data and relate their conclusions in hearings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Availability, recovery, and forensic analysis of VDR/hard-disk/camera data are critical evidentiary standards for technical investigations and legal proceedings; delays or seizure of such data can delay publication of technical reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigative authority and process for maritime accidents (CCISM role)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Italian Marine Casualty Investigation Central Board (Commissione centrale di indagine sui sinistri marittimi, CCISM), a unit of the Corps of the Port Captaincies – Coast Guard, conducts the technical investigations of maritime accidents and incidents within Italian-controlled waters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identifies the statutory investigative body and procedures; used to determine jurisdiction, scope and timeliness expectations for technical accident reports and whether international requests for publication are reasonable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criminal liability specifications for officers (manslaughter/abandonment/failure to inform)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prosecutors charged the captain and officers with manslaughter and violations of the Italian Penal Code and Code of Navigation for 'having caused the shipwreck owing to ... imprudence, negligence and incompetence' resulting in deaths; for abandoning incapacitated passengers; and for failing to inform maritime authorities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Legal standards and charge categories that define conduct giving rise to criminal liability in maritime disasters; these are the legal criteria judges and prosecutors apply when evaluating officer conduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Crew qualification composition as a safety-related factor
rubrics_metrics.description: Reports indicated that most of the Costa Concordia's crew were entertainers or bartenders, not qualified seamen.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Crew composition and qualifications are used as an evaluative criterion for preparedness and the ability to conduct safe navigation and orderly evacuation; a mismatch between crew roles and safety-critical duties can be cited as contributory negligence or poor staffing practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corporate best-practice response after an incident (external review and training)
rubrics_metrics.description: Carnival Corporation announced its board would engage outside consultants in various disciplines, including emergency response, organisation, training and implementation, to conduct a comprehensive review of the accident and the company's procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Engaging independent external experts to review and reform emergency procedures is presented as a post-incident governance/best-practice standard for companies to demonstrate remediation and improved safety culture.
